description: The 20 January sit-in report says a group but supplies no attendance. Later or earlier workforce totals describe employees represented, not people physically present.
required_followup: Find an opened contemporary report, organizer post, or other direct evidence giving an attendance estimate for the 20 January sit-in; do not use workforce totals as a crowd count.

description: The principal 20 January Alakhbar page remains search_only: web open returned Cache miss, and a normal public HTTPS request failed locally at DNS resolution before connecting. This is not an observed publisher denial.
required_followup: Retry through an available ordinary public reader or locate a separate accessible contemporary report; do not bypass access controls.

description: Le360 published a 4 January story about recurring Amel-worker demonstrations and an undated “latest sit-in” at the presidency. Its event date and relationship to the 20 January TAAZOUR sit-in are not established.
required_followup: Search late December 2020 and early January 2021 for the presidency sit-in and determine its occurrence date, threshold, and whether it is a distinct action or related to the 20 January sit-in.

description: The search-only 20 January report does not document any of the seven state responses to that gathering.
required_followup: Seek event-specific reporting or an organizer account for negotiation/receipt, arrests, beatings, dispersal, explicit nonresponse, killings, or shootings; otherwise retain unknown.

description: A 13 January search-only report describes public-school contract teachers refusing to resume classes, but it does not establish a public assembly, its attendance, or a date of any gathering. It remains a labor-action lead, not a coded event.
required_followup: Open/corroborate the report or find contemporary union/news evidence showing whether teachers held a public assembly, the date and attendance, and whether a demand was directed to national policy; if it was only a work stoppage/refusal, do not code it as a public-assembly event.

description: A search-only report attributes a sit-in at the presidential palace to the General Union of Amal Program Workers and says it occurred “this Wednesday,” but the page date is not visible. It may be separate from, or related to, the dated TAAZOUR sit-in; no relationship or January ownership is established.
required_followup: Recover the page’s publication date or another contemporaneous source, determine the gathering date and size, and compare organizer/location/demands before deciding whether it belongs to January or is the same episode as E001.

description: The Koylal/Feralla evidence now includes an FPC retrospective claim that a sit-in occurred on 22 January (S013), an FPC report that the farmers threatened a sit-in (S008), and a secondary timeline dating that threat to 25 January (S016). The conflict may reflect different stages or actions; it is unresolved. A separate actual sit-in is reported for 22 February (S014).
required_followup: Seek contemporaneous January reports or organizer records to verify the Jan22 gathering and resolve the Jan25 threat account; determine attendance, duration, and event-specific responses. Keep the Feb22 gathering separate unless episode evidence establishes otherwise.

description: The FPC retrospective says a Koylal sit-in occurred on 22 January but gives no attendance number or qualitative crowd description, so the Mass Mobilization threshold remains unverified. The February crowd description cannot be borrowed.
required_followup: Find event-specific January 22 attendance estimates or a clearly qualifying description from a contemporary/independent source; do not substitute the number of villages, landowners, households, or February attendees.

description: A 1 January Al-Hurriya search-only article explicitly reports protests against closure of mining areas and says hundreds of prospectors plus union representatives came to the area, calling for authorities to intervene. The exact occurrence date remains unstated; web open returned Cache miss and a normal same-URL HTTPS retry failed before connecting because local DNS resolution failed; it is unclear whether “hundreds came” quantifies simultaneous protest participants, and the official Arabic agency profile confirms that Maaden Mauritania was a public industrial/commercial institution under ministerial technical supervision from 2020, but the exact protest occurrence date and the meaning of the crowd phrase remain unclear. The later Feb22 tax/ore-fee reporting concerns a separate action and is not corroboration for January.
required_followup: Seek an independent contemporary report or archived article establishing the protest occurrence date and whether “hundreds” refers to people assembled at the protest. The public-institution and ministerial-supervision relationship is confirmed by official S019; retain unknown attendance/date where no further evidence is found.

description: A Jan24 Watanicom result reports that education-union organizations planned sit-ins at wilaya/department buildings on the first day of teacher evaluation, plus a Jan26 press conference. No source yet establishes that the gatherings occurred or supplies attendance; nationwide plan wording does not establish one simultaneous national event. Follow-up phrase/date/outlet searches (Q073–Q080) repeated the plan and surfaced March Mauritanian and unrelated foreign teacher actions, but no January 26 Mauritanian execution report; the event remains unresolved.
required_followup: Search Jan26–28 contemporary local reporting and union statements to determine whether planned sit-ins actually occurred by location, the attendance at each gathering, state demands and any event-specific responses. Keep the announced plan separate from executed actions.

description: The RFI article republished by Le Journal Africa is dated 18 January and says 300 teachers attended a Sunday press conference transformed into a meeting, implying 17 January (candidate E004). It separately says a Ministry sit-in was planned for Monday, but no execution source is found. The RFI domain returned robots.txt block and the repost page returned Cache miss. The meeting venue/open-public status remain unknown.
required_followup: Seek independent or organizer corroboration of the Jan17 300-person meeting, precise venue/public access, and any event-specific response; separately determine whether the planned Monday Ministry sit-in occurred and whether it was distinct. Do not merge with E001 without shared-actor/location/date evidence.

description: A Jan8 Alakhbar video-result description says the service-provider teachers’ protest movement began on 21 December 2020 against contract extension. A Jan23 union statement says a strike was suspended. The opened Jan1 Alakhbar article (S027) documents a letter to the President, not a gathering. Together these sources do not establish a qualifying public assembly or its continuation in January; the Jan17 300-person meeting (E004) and planned Jan18 sit-in are distinct actions unless episode evidence shows otherwise.
required_followup: Seek organizer or contemporaneous records specifying the physical form, dates, and attendance of early-January actions and whether any public gathering continued from the December campaign. Keep a work stoppage or campaign activity separate from public-assembly continuations; do not merge with E004 or the planned Jan18 sit-in without evidence.

description: The service-provider teachers’ campaign began on 21 December 2020 according to a Jan8 interview result, and a Jan23 statement says a strike was suspended. These are December-origin campaign/work-stoppage records; they do not establish any qualifying January public assembly or a continuing physical gathering. They may be related to, but are not the same event as, the Jan17 meeting E004.
required_followup: Only add a continuation if contemporary evidence establishes a public gathering that physically carried into January under the project’s episode rule. Distinguish campaign duration, strike/work stoppage, and the discrete Jan17 meeting.
